what_this_is: a continuous zoom from a tracked embryo down to a single molecular machine. The POSITIONS at the molecular end are invented - there is no simulation of physics here - but every size, count, rate and spacing is a measured value with a source, so what is drawn correctly is separable from what is drawn merely plausibly.
the_honest_header: Two different kinds of picture are stitched together here. The embryo is a MEASUREMENT: those are real tracked cells from a published light-sheet dataset. Everything from the cell inwards is a DEPICTION built to measured dimensions. The viewer marks which is which at every level, because the two look equally convincing and are not equally trustworthy.

organism.label: Mouse preimplantation development, zygote to morula
organism.what_it_is: a reference trajectory assembled from published stage structure, to exercise the format against a real developmental series rather than an invented one

steps.why_not: expected exactly 2 daughters per parent; got counts [1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1] for 8 parent(s) and 16 daughter(s). The source records stages, not lineage, so nearest-centre assignment is a guess and this one did not come out two-to-one.

packing_impossibility.claim: n equal spheres of total volume V cannot fit inside a sphere of volume V, for any n > 1
packing_impossibility.source: pi/(3*sqrt(2)), the face-centred-cubic/hexagonal density; proved optimal by Hales (Kepler conjecture)
options: let the cells interpenetrate - what the worked example does
let the envelope grow by at least 1/0.7405^(1/3) ~ 1.105 in radius - honest geometry, wrong biology
stop drawing cells as spheres - correct, and not available to a format that stores a centre and a radius
packing_impossibility.what_the_embryo_does: it flattens the cells against one another. In a mouse embryo the 8-cell stage compacts, which is a change in cell shape and adhesion, not in cell volume. A centre-and-radius representation cannot express it, so the stage with the most interesting mechanics is the stage the depiction cannot draw.

measured_secondhand: the cell count at each stage
the stage times and their unit
derived: the radius-versus-separation relation, from constant union volume
the furrow depth, as a description of the drawn shape
provenance.the_sentence: This is a diagram of cleavage, not a measurement of one. The stage sequence and timing come from the source file; every position and radius in it is marked "depicted", and nothing computed here can turn a depicted position into a measured one.

not_modelled: cytokinesis. There is no contractile ring, no spindle, and no mechanism: the waist in this drawing is the geometry of two overlapping spheres, which happens to look like a furrow.
the timing WITHIN a division. The separation is driven by an easing function supplied by the caller; nothing here knows how long anaphase takes relative to telophase.

asynchrony. Real cleavage divisions in an embryo are not simultaneous, and blastomeres divide out of step from the 2-cell stage onward. This plan divides a whole stage at once because the source file records stages rather than per-cell division times.
anything about shape other than sphericity. Real blastomeres flatten against one another, and compaction at the 8-cell stage is a change in cell SHAPE and adhesion that a sphere cannot show.

coordinates.units_in_source: VOXEL INDICES, not microns. The repository records this study's physical pixel size as null, so no micron scale is asserted anywhere here.
coordinates.normalisation: centred on the centroid of all 222,071 detections and divided by the maximum radius, so the cloud fits a unit sphere

clock.frame_interval_source: Shah et al. 2019, Results: "we acquired a 300 um thick spherical shell around the embryo surface every 150 s". Verified in the full text in this run.
clock.why_null: UNRESOLVED, and it would have shipped as a confident wrong number. The study describes imaging "from 4-18 hpf" (verified in the full text), which is 14 h. This file has 420 frames at 150 s, which is 17.5 h. The two cannot both describe this file, so either frame 0 is not at 4 hpf or the recording runs past 18 hpf. Nothing read in this run states the absolute stage of frame 0, so the viewer shows ELAPSED time and not hours post fertilisation.
clock.a_hint_not_used: frame 0 holds 21 endoderm nuclei and endoderm specification begins around 6.5 hpf by sox17 expression, which would put frame 0 later than 4 hpf. That is an INFERENCE from cell counts, not a published figure, so it is recorded and not applied.
clock.what_would_settle_it: the per-frame timestamps, which are not in the tracking XML, or a statement of the first frame's stage from the depositors.

covers.note: the window is the study's claim about its method; the elapsed figure is this file's 420 frames at the published interval. See clock.why_null.

tracks.claim: MEASURED identity and motion. These are the only cells in this dataset whose path over time is a measurement.

cloud.layout: float16 little-endian, 3 per point (x y z), frames concatenated in order

measured_embryo.division_events_note: 142 tracks survive the minimum-length filter; 42 of them record a parent, but only 4 have that parent ALSO in the file, because the filter severed the rest. So 4 division(s) can be drawn as measured events. The filter, not the data, is the limit: a re-export keeping short tracks would recover far more.

count_growth.note: the detected-cell count rises over the recording. That rise IS division happening, but a count is not an event: without lineage links it says that cells divided, not which ones.

machines.name: Eukaryotic ribosome (80S)
machines.what_it_does: Reads a messenger RNA three letters at a time and joins the matching amino acids into a protein chain.

dimensions_nm.from: 4UG0, deposited coordinates (deposited chains 81 = assembly 1 chains 81, so no expansion needed)
dimensions_nm.shape_note: Nearly isotropic: the longest and shortest principal extents differ by only about 15%. Drawing it as a lumpy sphere about 30 nm across is defensible; drawing it as an elongated object is not.

biological_object.null_reason: No independent mass measurement (analytical ultracentrifugation or native mass spectrometry) for the human 80S was retrieved this session.
biological_object.what_would_resolve_it: A native-MS or sedimentation-equilibrium mass for the intact human 80S, which would also say which associated factors were counted.

copies_per_cell.null_reason: No primary measurement of ribosomes per cell for any mammalian cell type was retrieved this session. Several searches returned nothing usable, and the commonly repeated "about ten million per mammalian cell" was not traced to a measurement.
copies_per_cell.what_would_resolve_it: An absolute quantification in a named cell line - rRNA mass per cell divided by rRNA mass per ribosome, or a calibrated ribosome-protein copy number - reported for a stated growth state. It must name the cell type: a ribosome count is a function of how fast the cell is growing.

rate.units: amino acids per second per ribosome
rate.conditions: in vivo; harringtonine block of initiation followed by ribosome run-off, tracked by ribosome profiling; a ~60 s delay for drug engagement was subtracted
rate.caveat: A population average over thousands of genes. The same paper reports more than a thousand sites where local ribosome density is 25-fold above the gene median, i.e. pauses of several seconds. The average is not what any one ribosome is doing at any one codon.

machines.verified_how: Fetched https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/4UG0 and read back title "STRUCTURE OF THE HUMAN 80S RIBOSOME", method ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, resolution_combined [3.6], molecular_weight 3835.52 kDa, 81 polymer entity instances, and source organism Homo sapiens from the polymer entities. Fetched assembly 1 and read back 81 polymer instances, so the deposited file is the whole particle. Downloaded 4ug0.cif.gz and measured 218,776 atoms. Fetched rcsb_primary_citation and read back DOI 10.1038/nature14427, PMID 25901680. Rate from the PMC full text of Ingolia 2011, quoted verbatim in SOURCES.

machines.name: Bacterial ribosome (70S)
machines.what_it_does: The same job as the eukaryotic ribosome - turning a messenger RNA into a protein - in a smaller machine with fewer parts.

dimensions_nm.shape_note: Smaller than the 80S in every principal direction, but only by about 11% on the longest axis. The two ribosomes are not dramatically different in size, which is the point of carrying both: a viewer that draws the bacterial one as half the size is wrong.

biological_object.null_reason: No independent mass measurement retrieved this session.
biological_object.what_would_resolve_it: A native-MS or sedimentation mass for the intact 70S, with the associated factors it counted stated.

copies_per_cell.strain: K-12 derivative AFS55, chromosomal S2-YFP replacing S2
copies_per_cell.growth_state: EZ rich defined medium, 30 C, bulk doubling time 54 min
copies_per_cell.counts: 30S subunits plus complete 70S ribosomes, because the label is on a small-subunit protein
copies_per_cell.method: total pre-bleach YFP intensity scaled to the intensity of a single YFP molecule
copies_per_cell.caveat: Increases monotonically with cell volume within the same culture. A single number per species does not exist; this one belongs to this strain in this medium at this temperature.

copies_per_cell.growth_state: 37 C, interpolated between 40 min and 60 min doubling times
copies_per_cell.method: earlier bulk measurement, reported second-hand by bakshi_2012 as the value their result disagrees with
copies_per_cell.caveat: THIS IS A SECOND-HAND NUMBER. It is recorded because the disagreement is threefold and real, not because the original was retrieved. The original measurement was not fetched this session. See DISAGREEMENTS.

rate.units: amino acids per second per ribosome
rate.conditions: fast growth, mu = 1.3 and 2.0 doublings per hour; kinetics of radioactive labelling of nascent and finished polypeptides

rate.units: amino acids per second per ribosome
rate.conditions: slow growth, mu = 0.67 doublings per hour; same method
rate.caveat: The rate is a function of growth rate, so a viewer that animates one speed is animating one growth condition. The same paper puts the engaged fraction of ribosomes at about 0.8 across all three growth rates, so roughly one ribosome in five is doing nothing at any instant.

machines.verified_how: Fetched the RCSB entry for 7K00 and read back title "Structure of the Bacterial Ribosome at 2 Angstrom Resolution", method ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, resolution_combined [1.98], molecular_weight 2209.99 kDa, 56 polymer instances, source organism Escherichia coli, and EMDB id EMD-22586. Fetched https://www.ebi.ac.uk/emdb/api/entry/EMD-22586 and read back title "Structure of the Bacterial Ribosome at 2 Angstrom Resolution (composite structure)", method singleParticle, resolution 1.98 A reported BY AUTHOR. Fetched assembly 1: 56 polymer instances, so no expansion. Downloaded 7k00.cif.gz and measured 149,338 atoms. Primary citation read back as DOI 10.7554/eLife.60482, PMID 32924932. Counts from the PMC full text of Bakshi 2012; rates from the PubMed abstract of Young & Bremer 1976, both quoted verbatim in SOURCES.

machines.name: RNA polymerase II
machines.what_it_does: Opens the DNA double helix and copies a gene into a messenger RNA, one nucleotide at a time.

dimensions_nm.from: 5FLM, deposited coordinates (transcribing mammalian Pol II; deposited chains 15 = assembly 1 chains 15)
dimensions_nm.shape_note: Compact and close to isotropic at this resolution. The 10-subunit yeast crystal form 1I3Q measures 14.9 x 13.2 x 12.8 nm with a 15.1 nm maximum extent over 28,161 atoms - smaller, because it has five fewer chains and no nucleic acid, not because the enzyme is smaller in that organism.
dimensions_nm.second_structure_note: Both numbers are kept. Choosing one and calling it "the" size of Pol II would hide the fact that the difference is a difference in what was crystallised.

deposited_model.source: rcsb_entry_info.molecular_weight for 5FLM = 548.25 kDa; for 1I3Q it is 470.17 kDa

biological_object.null_reason: No independent mass measurement of an intact Pol II elongation complex was retrieved this session.
biological_object.what_would_resolve_it: A native-MS mass for a defined elongation complex, stating which subunits and nucleic acids were present.

copies_per_cell.units: RNA polymerase II molecules per nucleus
copies_per_cell.null_reason: No primary measurement of Pol II copy number for any mammalian or fungal cell was retrieved this session.
copies_per_cell.what_would_resolve_it: A calibrated single-molecule count or absolute proteomic quantification of RPB1 in a named cell line and growth state. Note that the useful number is the number ENGAGED, not the number present, and those differ.

copies_per_cell.growth_state: EZ rich defined medium, 30 C, doubling time 43 min
copies_per_cell.method: total pre-bleach GFP intensity scaled to a single GFP molecule
copies_per_cell.caveat: THIS IS THE BACTERIAL ENZYME, NOT POL II. Bacteria have one multisubunit RNA polymerase; eukaryotes have three, of which Pol II makes messenger RNA. The number is carried here as the only polymerase count that was actually retrieved, and it is explicitly not a Pol II number.

rate.conditions: late gene body, 25-50 min after release from a flavopiridol pause block, tracked by GRO-seq; average over 245 measured rates, SD 0.79 kb/min
mid gene body, 12.5-25 min window; average over 938 measured rates, SD 0.69 kb/min
early gene body, 5-12.5 min window; average over 141 measured rates, SD 0.43 kb/min
rate.caveat: The polymerase ACCELERATES through a gene. The same paper fits a model running from 5 bp/s at the start site to 40 bp/s by 60 kb in - an eightfold change within one transcript. Any animation that moves a polymerase at a constant speed is showing something that was measured not to happen.

rate.conditions: across approximately 1000 genes and across regions within genes
rate.caveat: The same paper notes that earlier single-gene work across various organisms gave 1 to 4 kb/min, so the spread is not an artefact of one method.

machines.verified_how: Fetched the RCSB entries for 5FLM and 1I3Q. Read back for 5FLM: title "Structure of transcribing mammalian RNA polymerase II", method ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, resolution [3.4], 548.25 kDa, 15 polymer instances, source organisms Bos taurus and synthetic construct, EMDB EMD-3218, primary citation DOI 10.1038/NATURE16482 / PMID 26789250. For 1I3Q: title "RNA POLYMERASE II CRYSTAL FORM I AT 3.1 A RESOLUTION", X-RAY DIFFRACTION, resolution [3.1], 470.17 kDa, 10 polymer instances, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, DOI 10.1126/science.1059493 / PMID 11313498. Both assemblies match their deposited chain counts. Downloaded both coordinate files and measured them. Rates from the PMC full text of Jonkers 2014, quoted verbatim in SOURCES.

machines.name: DNA polymerase delta holoenzyme (lagging strand)
machines.what_it_does: Copies one of the two DNA strands during cell division, clamped onto the DNA by a ring that stops it falling off.
machines.which_polymerase: Pol delta. The leading and lagging strands are copied by DIFFERENT enzymes and this matters for a viewer that draws a replication fork: Pol epsilon is generally assigned to the leading strand and Pol delta to the lagging strand. A fork drawn with the same enzyme on both sides is drawing a model nobody holds. The separate entry dna_polymerase_epsilon_holoenzyme carries the other one.

dimensions_nm.shape_note: Distinctly flattened: the shortest principal extent is two thirds of the longest. The particle is the four-subunit polymerase sitting on the trimeric sliding clamp, with a primer-template duplex threaded through - so the envelope includes DNA, not just protein.

biological_object.null_reason: No independent mass measurement of a Pol delta holoenzyme was retrieved this session.
biological_object.what_would_resolve_it: A native-MS mass for the assembled holoenzyme, stating whether the clamp and the primer-template were counted.

copies_per_cell.null_reason: No primary measurement retrieved this session.
copies_per_cell.what_would_resolve_it: An absolute quantification of POLD1 in a named cell line, with the cell cycle phase stated - the number in a cell that is not replicating its DNA is not the number in one that is.

rate.cell_type: normal primary keratinocytes pooled from three donors
rate.conditions: single-molecule DNA combing of pulse-labelled replication tracks; the velocity is of the FORK, i.e. of a polymerase pair with its helicase, not of an isolated enzyme
rate.caveat: The distribution is wide and right-skewed: the extremes span almost two orders of magnitude, so the mean is a poor summary and is reported here with the median, the SD and the range rather than alone.
Faster than the primary cells in the same experiment, significantly so by the authors' own t test. A transformed line is not a normal cell for this purpose.

rate.quantity: nucleotide incorporation by the isolated enzyme
rate.null_reason: No in vitro turnover number for human Pol delta was retrieved this session.
rate.what_would_resolve_it: A steady-state or single-turnover kinetic measurement on the purified holoenzyme, with the template, salt and temperature stated. It will not equal the in vivo fork rate, and the gap between the two is itself worth showing.

machines.verified_how: Fetched the RCSB entry for 6TNY and read back title "Processive human polymerase delta holoenzyme", method ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, resolution [3.08], 351.43 kDa, 9 polymer instances, source organisms Homo sapiens and synthetic construct, EMDB EMD-10539, primary citation DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-14898-6 / PMID 32111820. Fetched the polymer entities and read back the chain inventory recorded in STRUCTURES_VERIFIED, including a catalytic subunit of exactly 1107 residues. Assembly 1 matches the deposited chain count. Downloaded 6tny.cif.gz and measured 19,726 atoms. Fork rates from the PMC record of Conti 2007, quoted verbatim in SOURCES.

machines.name: DNA polymerase epsilon holoenzyme (leading strand)
machines.what_it_does: Copies the other DNA strand during cell division, travelling continuously behind the machine that unzips the double helix.
machines.which_polymerase: Pol epsilon, the four-subunit holoenzyme. The only structure retrieved for it is from a microbe, not a mammal; see the organism caveat on dimensions.

dimensions_nm.shape_note: The most elongated machine in this file: the longest principal extent is more than twice the shortest. Drawing it as a blob loses the one thing its shape says.
dimensions_nm.organism_caveat: THIS GEOMETRY IS FROM A MICROBE (Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C), not from a mammal. The Pol delta entry beside it is human. A viewer that places these two side by side at a mammalian replication fork is mixing organisms, and that mixing has to be on the label, not in a footnote. The 2222 modelled residues of the catalytic subunit belong to the yeast protein; no claim is made here that the mammalian enzyme has the same dimensions.

biological_object.null_reason: No independent mass measurement retrieved this session.
biological_object.what_would_resolve_it: A native-MS mass for the assembled four-subunit holoenzyme.

copies_per_cell.null_reason: No primary measurement retrieved this session, for either the fungal or the mammalian enzyme.
copies_per_cell.what_would_resolve_it: An absolute quantification of the catalytic subunit in a named organism, cell type and cell cycle phase.

rate.note: The fork rates on dna_polymerase_delta_holoenzyme are FORK rates and belong to both strands of the same fork. They are not duplicated here, because repeating a number in two places is how a single measurement gets counted twice downstream.

rate.quantity: leading-strand synthesis by the isolated holoenzyme
rate.null_reason: No in vitro turnover number for Pol epsilon was retrieved this session, in any organism.
rate.what_would_resolve_it: A kinetic measurement on the purified holoenzyme with the template, salt and temperature stated, ideally alongside the same measurement on Pol delta so the two strands can be compared on one axis.

machines.verified_how: Fetched the RCSB entry for 6WJV and read back title "Structure of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae polymerase epsilon holoenzyme", method ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, resolution [3.5], 379.21 kDa, 4 polymer instances, source organism Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C, EMDB EMD-21701. The primary citation came back with DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-16910-5 and journal/year Nat Commun 2020 but a NULL PubMed id, so no PMID is recorded. Read back the four-chain inventory including a 2222-residue catalytic subunit A. Assembly 1 matches the deposited chain count. Downloaded 6wjv.cif.gz and measured 19,593 atoms. For contrast, fetched https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q07864.json, which returned DPOE1_HUMAN, 2286 residues, 261,518 Da - the HUMAN catalytic subunit, confirming that the structure above is not the human protein.

machines.name: Nucleosome core particle
machines.what_it_does: A spool of eight histone proteins with about 147 base pairs of DNA wound round it, the unit that packs the genome and controls what can be read.

dimensions_nm.shape_note: A flattened disc: two comparable extents and a third half their size. This is the one machine in the file whose shape a viewer must get right, because the disc axis is what makes a chromatin fibre a fibre.
dimensions_nm.tails_caveat: These numbers INCLUDE the histone tails, which 1KX5 models at 1.94 A. The tails stick out well past the DNA gyres, which is why the maximum atom-pair distance (17.4 nm) is so much larger than the largest principal extent (14.4 nm). The lower-resolution 1AOI, with shorter modelled histone constructs, measures 13.6 x 11.5 x 7.0 nm with a 14.5 nm maximum over 12,385 atoms. The ordered core is smaller than either. Any single "nucleosome diameter" is answering a question about which atoms were modelled, not only about the particle.
dimensions_nm.textbook_figure_not_retrieved: The widely quoted disc diameter of about 10-11 nm was NOT traced to a primary measurement this session, so it is not asserted. What can be asserted is the envelope of the deposited coordinates above, and that it is larger than the quoted figure because it includes the tails. See TEXTBOOK_ONLY.

deposited_model.source: rcsb_entry_info.molecular_weight for 1KX5 = 200.28 kDa; for 1AOI it is 184.55 kDa

biological_object.null_reason: No independent mass measurement retrieved this session.
biological_object.what_would_resolve_it: A native-MS mass for a reconstituted core particle, stating the DNA length used.

dna_wrapped_bp.source: Read off the 1KX5 deposition: two polydeoxyribonucleotide entities of 147 nucleotides each, one per strand.

also.note: The 1997 structure used a 146 bp palindromic fragment, described by the deposition as "PALINDROMIC 146 BP DNA REPEAT 8/9 FROM HUMAN X-CHROMOSOME ALPHA SATELLITE DNA". 146 and 147 are both real: they are two different constructs, not two estimates of one quantity.

histone_stoichiometry.read_back: From the 1KX5 polymer entities: H3 x2, H4 x2, H2A.1 x2, H2B.2 x2. The octamer is read off the deposition, not assumed.
histone_stoichiometry.organism_note: The histones in both 1KX5 and 1AOI are from an amphibian (Xenopus laevis); the DNA in 1AOI is a human alpha-satellite sequence. The particle a mammalian viewer draws is therefore being drawn from a cross-organism reconstitution, which is standard practice and is still a mixing that belongs on the label.

copies_per_cell.null_reason: This cannot be computed without a nucleosome repeat length, and the repeat length is NOT A CONSTANT. Woodcock, Skoultchi & Fan 2006 report "a robust linear relationship between H1 stoichiometry and NRL" and that repeat length falls in H1-depleted nuclei, varying by cell type and organism. A single nucleosome count per cell would be asserting a repeat length nobody measured for that cell.
copies_per_cell.what_would_resolve_it: A measured nucleosome repeat length for the specific cell type being drawn, from micrococcal nuclease ladder spacing or an equivalent assay. With that, the count follows from the genome size below.

what_is_known.genome_note: Twice the sum of the 25 primary GRCh38.p14 chromosomes (3,088,286,401 bp), read from Ensembl REST release 116. Using the golden path length of 3,099,750,718 bp instead gives 6,199,501,436 bp. Both are recorded; the difference between them is under 0.4% and is swamped by the repeat-length uncertainty.
what_is_known.hard_upper_bound_note: Diploid genome divided by the 147 bp core wrap. This is the number of nucleosomes there would be if there were NO linker DNA at all, so it is a strict upper bound and not an estimate. The true count is lower by whatever the linker is, which is the quantity that was not retrieved. Stating the bound is not the same as stating the count, and this field must not be read as one.

rate.null_reason: No measurement of nucleosome turnover, unwrapping or remodeller-driven sliding rate was retrieved this session.
rate.what_would_resolve_it: A single-molecule unwrapping or FRAP-based turnover measurement in a named cell type. Note that a nucleosome is not a catalyst, so "rate" here means how fast it moves or comes apart, not how fast it converts a substrate.

For 1AOI: title "COMPLEX BETWEEN NUCLEOSOME CORE PARTICLE (H3,H4,H2A,H2B) AND 146 BP LONG DNA FRAGMENT", resolution [2.8], 184.55 kDa, Xenopus laevis, DOI 10.1038/38444 / PMID 9305837. Fetched the polymer entities of both and read back the chain-by-chain inventories in STRUCTURES_VERIFIED, from which the 147 bp wrap and the histone octamer are taken directly. Both assemblies match their deposited chain counts. Downloaded both coordinate files and measured them. Genome size from https://rest.ensembl.org/info/assembly/homo_sapiens, reading back assembly_name GRCh38.p14, accession GCA_000001405.29 and golden_path 3,099,750,718, with the per-chromosome lengths summed locally. Repeat-length caveat from the PubMed abstract of Woodcock 2006, quoted verbatim in SOURCES. machines.name: Nuclear pore complex
machines.what_it_does: A gateway through the double membrane around the nucleus that lets the right molecules in and out and keeps everything else where it belongs.

dimensions_nm.from: 7R5J, EXPANDED BIOLOGICAL ASSEMBLY 1 (C8, 808 polymer chains, 4,937,064 atoms). The deposited file holds 101 chains, one eighth of the ring, and must not be measured directly.
dimensions_nm.outer_diameter_method: Twice the largest in-plane distance of any atom from the ring axis (largest radius 79.8 nm). The axis was taken as the shortest bounding-box direction, which for a C8 ring is the symmetry axis.
dimensions_nm.bounding_box_note: Axis-aligned, which for this deposition is already the ring frame: the two in-plane extents agree to 0.1 nm, as an eightfold-symmetric ring measured in its own frame should. The agreement is a check on the arithmetic, not a finding.
dimensions_nm.max_extent_note: Greatest distance between any two modelled atoms, by the same two-pass farthest-point search used for every other entry, over all 4,937,064 atoms. It coincides with twice the largest in-plane radius to within the reported precision, which says the two extreme atoms lie in nearly the same plane - the pore is widest across its equator, not corner to corner.
dimensions_nm.scaffold_channel_method: Twice the SMALLEST in-plane radius of any atom (26.5 nm). This is the aperture of the modelled scaffold, not the functional aperture; the disordered nucleoporins that fill the channel are not in the model.
dimensions_nm.spoke_note: The single asymmetric unit measures 82.9 x 77.2 x 52.5 nm with a 92.4 nm maximum atom-pair distance over 617,133 atoms. Those numbers describe one eighth of the pore and are recorded only so the mistake of using them is visible.
dimensions_nm.conformational_state: DILATED. 7R5J is the dilated state; the constricted state is a separate deposition (7TBL / EMD-14322, read back as "Human nuclear pore complex (constricted)" at 12 A). The pore breathes, so "the diameter of the nuclear pore" is not one number.
dimensions_nm.disagreement_note: The 159.7 nm measured here is larger than the figure commonly quoted for this complex. See DISAGREEMENTS; the quoted figure was not traced to a primary measurement this session and is therefore not written down as a rival number.

deposited_model.source: rcsb_entry_info.molecular_weight for 7R5J = 12078.34 kDa - the ONE asymmetric unit that the file contains, not the ring.

biological_object.read_back: From the retrieved abstract: "With a molecular weight of ~120 MDa, the human NPC is one of the largest protein complexes."

atomic_model_coverage.read_back: "Our 70-MDa atomically resolved model covers >90% of the human NPC scaffold." So roughly 50 MDa of the complex is not in any atomic model - it is the disordered part.

mass_MDa.why_three_numbers: The deposited file, the atomic scaffold model and the biological complex are three different objects. Reporting one of them as "the mass of the nuclear pore complex" would be wrong whichever one was chosen.

total_protein_chains.read_back: "Its ~1000 proteins are taken in multiple copies"

span.note: The whole molecular scale this viewer draws spans this one factor - just under a single order of magnitude. And it is not spread evenly: every machine except the nuclear pore falls inside a factor of 2.2 of every other, and then there is one gap of more than fourfold to the pore. So the honest picture is a tight cluster and one outlier, not a ladder with even rungs. A viewer that spaces these objects evenly for legibility is inventing the spacing.

size_ladder.not_a_score: Every number returned here is a length in nanometres or a ratio of two such lengths. There is no fused quality, confidence or fidelity value anywhere in this return.

what_a_depiction_cannot_show.headline: Everything below is true of every molecular illustration ever published, including this one. It is listed because a viewer that zooms smoothly from an embryo to a ribosome invites a reader to believe they are looking through a microscope, and they are not.
what_a_depiction_cannot_show.it_is_not_a_static_object: A drawn machine has one shape. A real one does not. The ribosome ratchets between conformations on every elongation cycle; the polymerase opens and closes its clamp; the spliceosome rebuilds its own catalytic core partway through the reaction it is catalysing, which is why the entry above has to name a state. The single most honest thing a drawing of a molecular machine can do is say WHICH STATE it is drawing, and the second most honest is to admit that the machine spends only part of its time there. Where this file could name the state, it did (the spliceosome "just prior to exon ligation"; the nuclear pore "dilated"). Where it could not, the omission is the limitation.
what_a_depiction_cannot_show.the_surface_is_a_threshold_not_a_boundar: A cryo-EM structure is a three-dimensional map of electron scattering density. It has no surface. The surface you see in any rendering is an ISOSURFACE: the locus of points where that density equals a number somebody chose. Raise the threshold and the molecule shrinks; lower it and it grows and sprouts features. For a crystal structure the situation is different but not better: the atoms have positions, and the "surface" is then a set of spheres of chosen radii rolled over with a probe of chosen size. In neither case is there a line in nature where the molecule stops. The envelopes in this file are extents of MODELLED ATOM CENTRES, which at least has an unambiguous definition, and are therefore slightly smaller than any rendered surface of the same structure.
what_a_depiction_cannot_show.what_is_modelled_is_not_what_is_there: A structure contains only the parts that held still enough to be resolved. The nuclear pore above is the clearest case: the atomic model covers roughly 70 of about 120 MDa, and the missing 50 MDa is not missing from the cell - it is the disordered nucleoporin mesh that fills the channel and does the actual gatekeeping. A drawing faithful to the coordinates shows an open hole where the functional part of the machine is. The opposite error appears in the nucleosome, where the 1.94 A structure DOES model the histone tails, so its envelope is larger than the particle a lower-resolution structure would give. In both directions, the drawing inherits the experiment's blind spots and calls them geometry.
what_a_depiction_cannot_show.it_diffuses: At this scale thermal motion dominates. A ribosome in the cytoplasm is not parked; it is being battered from every side and wandering. One of the few numbers retrieved here that bears on this is a measured diffusion coefficient of about 0.04 square micrometres per second for ribosomes in a live microbial cell (Bakshi et al. 2012, attributed by the authors to free messenger RNA being translated by one or more ribosomes). A viewer that holds its machines still for the reader to look at is removing the single most prominent feature of their actual behaviour. A viewer that animates them as gliding smoothly along a track is worse, because smooth gliding is what thermal motion is not.
what_a_depiction_cannot_show.it_is_crowded: Illustrations place machines in empty space because machines in a crowd are unreadable. The cell is the crowd. The same superresolution study puts about 55,000 ribosomes in one microbial cell and finds them packed densely enough in the ribosome-rich regions that the authors discuss the biopolymer volume fraction; it also finds the ribosomes and the DNA strongly segregated, so even the emptiness is structured rather than uniform. Every number in this file was measured on a purified, isolated complex. None of them was measured in the crowd the drawing leaves out.
what_a_depiction_cannot_show.the_positions_are_invented: Nothing in this module says where anything is. The viewer must put each object somewhere, and every such placement is generated. That is not a defect to be fixed by better data; there is no measurement of the instantaneous arrangement of machines in a particular cell to fix it with. The requirement is that the placement be LABELLED as generated while the size beside it is labelled as measured, which is what the sibling module provenance.mjs exists to enforce.
what_a_depiction_cannot_show.rates_are_averages_over_populations: Every rate in this file is a population average, and in each case the paper it came from reports a distribution wide enough that the average misleads. Translation elongation averages 5.6 amino acids per second in one mammalian cell type, with more than a thousand sites where the ribosome pauses for seconds. Replication forks average 1.46 kb/min with individual forks from 0.14 to 11.8 kb/min, a spread of nearly two orders of magnitude. Transcription accelerates eightfold within a single gene. An animation playing at the mean speed is showing a motion that no individual machine performs.
what_a_depiction_cannot_show.one_organism_is_not_another: The entries above are drawn from a mammal, two microbes and an amphibian, and the reason is availability, not biology. The leading-strand polymerase in this file is a fungal structure sitting next to a human lagging-strand polymerase at a notional mammalian fork. The nucleosome is amphibian histones on human satellite DNA. These are the standard reagents of structural biology and the structures are good; the mixing is still a mixing, and a viewer that presents the assembled scene as one organism's chromosome is asserting something no experiment did.

superhelical_turns.disagreement: The widely quoted figure is 1.65 turns. Computing the azimuth of one strand about the best-fit axis of the deposited coordinates gives 1.81 turns in 1AOI and 1.805 in 1KX5. These are almost certainly different definitions - a superhelical parameter fitted to the tightly bound core versus a total azimuthal sweep that includes the flared ends - but no primary sentence defining the 1.65 figure was retrieved in this session, so it is not asserted here as a measurement. The computed 1.81 is.

chromatin_levels.name: 30 nm fibre

dimension.null_reason: There is no single diameter to report, because the in-vitro object and the in-situ object are not the same object. In vitro the measured diameters are two discrete classes, 33 nm and 44 nm, depending on linker length. In situ no periodicity above ~11 nm is detectable at all, and the measured fibre diameters form one broad distribution centred near 17 nm. Reporting "30 nm" would be reporting neither.
dimension.what_would_resolve_it: an in-situ method that resolves individual fibres in unperturbed nuclei AND detects a 30 nm periodicity. ChromEM tomography is the closest existing method and it reports the opposite.

bp_per_nm.what: For the in-vitro 33 nm class only: 11 nucleosomes per 11 nm is exactly one nucleosome per nanometre of fibre axis, so the base pairs per nanometre equal the nucleosome repeat length. Combined with the mouse embryonic stem cell repeat length of 183.4 bp this gives 183.4 bp/nm.
bp_per_nm.the_splice_is_the_weakness: The linear density was measured on a reconstitution with defined linkers; the repeat length was measured in mouse embryonic stem cells. Multiplying them assumes the fibre in the cell has the reconstitution's linear density, which is the very thing in dispute. Use this number to show what the textbook fibre WOULD compact to, never as a property of a nucleus.

chromatin_levels.organism: none for the in-vitro structures - reconstituted arrays. Homo sapiens for every in-situ test.
chromatin_levels.organism_note: A reconstituted array has no cell type, no growth state and no genome. The histone preparation behind the best linear-density measurement is not mammalian, and a mammalian reconstitution is a different experiment. This is the entry on the ladder where "which organism" has no answer, and that is itself part of the problem.
chromatin_levels.cell_type: not applicable in vitro; human mitotic chromosomes and interphase nuclei in situ
chromatin_levels.evidence: IN VITRO: long regularly folded fibres reconstituted from nucleosome arrays with linker histone give two discrete diameter classes with unexpectedly high nucleosome density, and an 11 A cryo-EM reconstruction of such a fibre shows a histone-H1-dependent left-handed twist of tetranucleosomal units. IN SITU: cryo-EM of vitreous sections shows no 30 nm fibres and no 30 nm signal in the power spectra; small-angle X-ray scattering detects no structural feature larger than 11 nm; electron tomography inside cells shows a disordered 5-24 nm chain. MIXED: focused-ion-beam dissection of a metaphase chromosome finds fibres up to 30 nm present but in the minority of a 5-25 nm distribution, with no higher-order periodicity.

thirty_nm_problem.one_sentence: Regular 30 nm chromatin fibres are a reproducible, structurally solved property of reconstituted nucleosome arrays, and no method that looks inside an undisturbed nucleus has found them in bulk chromatin; so a viewer that draws a solenoid between the beads-on-a-string and the chromosome is drawing an in-vitro object in an in-vivo place.
thirty_nm_problem.what_is_not_in_dispute: Four things. (1) Nucleosomes exist, wrap about 147 bp, and are spaced by short linkers. (2) Under low ionic strength and with linker histone present, purified nucleosome arrays fold into regular fibres whose diameter has been measured and whose structure has been reconstructed by cryo-EM. (3) Inside a cell, chromatin is dense - between about a fifth and a half of the local volume - and irregular. (4) Chromatin is not static: single nucleosomes in living mammalian cells move about 50 nm every 30 ms. No side of the argument disputes any of these.
thirty_nm_problem.what_is_actually_in_dispute: Whether the regular fibre is a LEVEL OF ORGANISATION in a nucleus, or a state that purified chromatin adopts when it is diluted enough to have room to adopt it. The in-situ side does not claim the 30 nm fibre is a crystallographic error; the Maeshima reviews say explicitly that chromatin ranges "from an extended 10-nm fiber, to a folded 30-nm fiber, to chromatin condensates" depending on the ionic environment. The claim is narrower and harder to escape: in a nucleus at physiological crowding, the 10 nm chain is interdigitated with its neighbours rather than folded on itself, so there is no 30 nm repeat to find.
thirty_nm_problem.the_evidence_for_the_fibre: Finch and Klug 1976 saw extracted nucleofilaments of about 100 A condense, in 0.2 mM magnesium, into a solenoid of pitch about 110 A, and correlated it with a 300 A thread reported by others - note that the famous 30 nm is the correlated thread, not the measured pitch. Robinson and colleagues in 2006 reconstituted long regular fibres with defined linkers and measured two discrete diameter classes, 33 nm and 44 nm, at unexpectedly high nucleosome densities of 11 and 15 nucleosomes per 11 nm. Schalch and colleagues solved a tetranucleosome at 9 A, and Song and colleagues reconstructed a whole fibre at 11 A showing a linker-histone-dependent left-handed twist of tetranucleosomal units. These are real measurements of a real object.
thirty_nm_problem.the_evidence_against_it_being_in_cells: Eltsov and colleagues in 2008 imaged high-pressure-frozen human mitotic cells by cryo-electron microscopy of vitreous sections, with no stain, no fixative and the contrast transfer function computationally corrected, and found a homogeneous grainy texture with no visible 30 nm fibres and no 30 nm signal in the power spectra. Joti and colleagues in 2012 applied small-angle X-ray scattering, which detects periodicity in non-crystalline material without imaging it at all, and found no structural feature larger than 11 nm anywhere up to a chromosome-diameter scale of about a micrometre, with the same result in interphase nuclei up to about 275 nm. Ou and colleagues in 2017 stained DNA with a dye that polymerises into an electron-dense deposit and did tomography on intact cells, and found a disordered curvilinear chain of 5 to 24 nm. Three methods with different failure modes agree.
thirty_nm_problem.the_study_that_splits_the_difference: Wako and colleagues in 2020 dissected a single human metaphase chromosome every 10 nm into 224 cross-sections by focused ion beam and SEM. They found both 11 nm and 30 nm fibres. But the mean diameter was 16.9 nm with a standard deviation of 8.2 nm, the majority lay between 5 and 25 nm, fibres at 30 nm were a minority, and no higher-order periodical structure was detectable. The title is the fairest summary anyone has written: a chromosome of randomly arranged fibres with UP TO 30 nm diameter. "Up to" is not "of".
thirty_nm_problem.why_the_textbook_figure_persists: Because it is the only level of the hierarchy that explains how you get from a 10 nm chain to a micrometre-scale chromosome in a tidy number of steps, and because a diagram needs a step there. The in-situ answer - that the chain is irregular, interdigitated, locally fluid and compacted by crowding rather than by folding - is correct and undrawable. The 30 nm solenoid survives because it is illustratable, which is exactly the wrong reason for a viewer to adopt it.
what_a_viewer_should_therefore_draw: Draw a chain of nucleosomes whose apparent thickness VARIES along its length within 5-24 nm, not a fibre of one diameter.
Do not draw a solenoid, a zigzag, or any repeating higher-order coil in a nucleus. There is no measured periodicity above about 11 nm in situ to justify one.
Compact by crowding: let neighbouring chains interdigitate and fill the volume, rather than by winding one chain onto itself. That is the in-situ picture and it is also easier to generate.
Target a chromatin volume fraction, which IS measured: about 30% (range 12-52%) in an interphase nucleus and about 42% (range 35-47%) in a mitotic chromosome.

If the regular 30 nm fibre is shown at all, show it as a labelled in-vitro inset - a reconstitution in a test tube - at 33 nm or 44 nm according to linker length, never as a rung of the in-vivo ladder.
Animate it. A still frame of chromatin at any diameter implies a rigidity that single-nucleosome tracking in living cells contradicts at about 50 nm per 30 ms.
Say on the screen which rungs are measured and which are generated. The whole purpose of separating this module from the renderer is that the answer can be shown rather than assumed.
thirty_nm_problem.what_would_settle_it: A method that resolves individual chromatin fibres in an unperturbed nucleus AND tests for a 30 nm periodicity in the same data, over a volume large enough to contain many repeats. ChromEM tomography is the closest existing instrument and it reports against. A positive result from a method with different artefacts - not another reconstitution - is what would move this entry off CONTESTED.

The same paper elsewhere describes "a typical elongation rate of ~6 codons per second" when reasoning about pause durations. 5.6 is the measured figure; ~6 is a rounding used in prose, and the two must not be stacked as independent values.
Local rate is far from uniform: the paper finds pause sites with 25-fold or greater ribosome density, lasting seconds. An animation at a constant 5.6 aa/s depicts the mean and erases the pauses.

replication_fork_bacteria.mechanistic_anchor: The same paper reports a dnaE173 mutant fork at 264 +/- 9 nt/s, with that mutant Pol III elongating at 300 nt/s against 900 nt/s for wild-type Pol III. So the fork runs at roughly two thirds of the bare polymerase rate, and the polymerase is the rate-determining part.
replication_fork_bacteria.contrast_with_mammal: About 22-fold faster than the mammalian fork figure above (653 vs about 30 bp/s). An animation tuned to one is wrong for the other by more than an order of magnitude.
caveats: A purpose-built thymidine-requiring strain is not wild-type E. coli, and analogue incorporation is the premise of the assay rather than a control for it.

Fork velocity in bacteria is neither constant along the chromosome nor constant in time: Huang et al. 2023 report locus-dependent velocity, brief pauses at ribosomal DNA loci in wild-type cells, and temporal oscillations of roughly 0.5 peak-to-peak relative amplitude with a 10 to 15 min period in three species. A single value is a mean over that structure.

transcription_bacteria.method: in vivo timing on a plasmid-borne lacZ reporter under a T7 A1 promoter; Table 1
transcription_bacteria.verified_how: PubMed MCP metadata for PMID 20413502 plus a live fetch of the PMC page, which returned a transcription elongation rate of 42 nt/s with a matching translation elongation rate of 14 aa/s for E. coli MG1655 in exponential LB growth, and Table 1 values of 21 nt/s with 7 aa/s in stationary phase and 31 nt/s with 10 aa/s on glycerol.
transcription_bacteria.coupling: In the same experiment the transcription rate TRACKS the translation rate condition by condition: 42 with 14, 31 with 10, 21 with 7. The paper's claim is that the trailing ribosome sets the polymerase's pace by preventing backtracking. For an animation this means the bacterial polymerase and the bacterial ribosome are not independently tunable.
transcription_bacteria.corroborating_direction: Vogel and Jensen 1994 independently found the E. coli RNA chain elongation rate to fall by 40% when growth rate fell four-fold, and always to correlate with translation elongation - the same direction, from a different lab and method. Their absolute nt/s values could not be read (the 1994 issue is page images in PMC), so only the direction is claimed from them.
caveats: A plasmid reporter under a phage promoter is not a chromosomal gene.

Vogel and Jensen 1994 also report that an untranslated ribosomal RNA chain elongates nearly twice as fast as mRNA, so "the bacterial transcription rate" depends on whether the transcript is being translated at all.

cleavage_stage_embryo_cycles.what: cycle durations during the rapid cleavage divisions of an early embryo, before the midblastula transition
cleavage_stage_embryo_cycles.the_structural_point: These cycles are short and lack gap phases: the cycle is replication and division with little or nothing between them. Farrell and O'Farrell 2014 (a REVIEW) states that many embryos "begin development with extremely short cell cycles that exhibit unusually rapid DNA replication and no gap phases", and that the slowdown at the midblastula transition works by extending S phase and introducing a post-replicative G2. That is the reason the cultured-cell quartet above cannot be reused for an embryo.

whole_genome_one_origin.caveat: A genome is not one molecule, so one origin for a whole genome is not even geometrically possible. This figure is the scale of the problem, not a scenario.

chromosome_1_one_origin.why_this_is_the_fair_version: Chromosome 1 IS one DNA molecule, so a single origin on it is a scenario that could physically obtain. Two forks, each copying half of 248,956,422 bp.

the_inequality.statement: Both ratios are far greater than 1. That is the whole argument. The fastest retrieved fork rate and the longest retrieved S phase - the pairing most favourable to a single origin - still leave it short by orders of magnitude.

floor_on_the_origin_count.what_it_is: The fewest origins that could finish inside the longest observed S phase if all of them fired at once and no fork ever stopped.
floor_on_the_origin_count.what_it_is_not: An estimate of how many origins a cell fires. A cell fires more, because origins fire throughout S rather than simultaneously and because forks terminate on meeting. Petryk et al. 2016 showed that initiation in the human genome is stochastic within broad zones up to 150 kb wide rather than at a fixed set of points, so "the number of origins" is not even a single well-defined quantity.

whole_process_at_real_time.reading: The molecules are nearly real-time-animatable. The processes they belong to are not: one S phase in real time is millions of frames, and even the shortest sourced embryonic nuclear cycle is tens of thousands. So a viewer that zooms from embryo to chromosome crosses a boundary where the time axis must be cut, and the honest design is to show the molecular speed truthfully and to state the compression factor on the cell-scale view rather than to pick one rate for both.

source: Chen, Y., Hulsmann, J.E., et al. (2023) Estimating Total Quantitative Protein Content in Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and HeLa Cells. Int J Mol Sci 24:2081. (PMC9916689). Milo, R. (2013) What is the total number of protein molecules per cell volume? A call to rethink some published values. BioEssays 35:1050-1055. doi:10.1002/bies.201300066 (PMID 24114984, PMC3910158). mammalian.source: Milo, R. (2013) What is the total number of protein molecules per cell volume? A call to rethink some published values. BioEssays 35:1050-1055. doi:10.1002/bies.201300066 (PMID 24114984, PMC3910158). Estimates 2-4 million proteins per cubic micron for microbes, yeast and mammalian cells; reports a mammalian protein density of about 0.2 g/mL and mammalian cell-line volumes of 2,000-4,000 um^3; finds measured proteomics values for mammalian cells 3-10x LOWER than the estimate and says so.
mammalian.verified_how: Read in the full text of PMC3910158: "For mammalian cells, a value for protein density of ~0.2 g/mL was reported". The same text records an outlier of 60 mg/mL in the literature and states it is not considered representative.
mammalian.what_is_missing_from_it: RNA, DNA, lipid and the glycan mass. A total-macromolecule figure for a mammalian cytoplasm would be higher than 0.2 g/mL by an amount this file cannot quantify.

total_macromolecule_mass_concentration_m.null_reason: No measurement of TOTAL macromolecule concentration in a mammalian cytoplasm, comparable to Zimmerman & Trach 1991 for a microbe, was retrieved this session. The 0.2 g/mL above is protein only.
total_macromolecule_mass_concentration_m.what_would_resolve_it: A quantitative dry-mass or refractive-index measurement on a named mammalian cell type reporting total macromolecule mass per cell volume, or the Zimmerman-Trach extraction protocol applied to one.

qualitative_corroboration.statement: The aqueous phase of cytoplasm is crowded rather than dilute, and as much as half the cellular protein may be in a solid phase.
qualitative_corroboration.source: Luby-Phelps, K. (2000) Cytoarchitecture and physical properties of cytoplasm: volume, viscosity, diffusion, intracellular surface area. Int Rev Cytol 192:189-221. doi:10.1016/s0074-7696(08)60527-6 (PMID 10553280). Review; its abstract states that the aqueous phase of cytoplasm "is crowded rather than dilute" and that as much as half the cellular protein may be in a solid phase.
qualitative_corroboration.verified_how: Fetched the PubMed record for PMID 10553280 and read the abstract.
qualitative_corroboration.why_only_qualitative: A review abstract. It corroborates the direction and supplies no number this file could use.

microbe_total_macromolecules.note: Low end: 0.3 g/mL at the small specific volume. High end: 0.4 g/mL at the large one. The interval is wide because both the concentration and the conversion are.

mammalian_protein_only.note: PROTEIN only. The true macromolecular fraction of a mammalian cell is above this and is not quantified here.

protein_spacing.method: cube root of the volume per particle; a lattice idealisation, not a measurement

molecular.cell_self_consistency: The sourced cell volume and the sourced nuclear volume are NOT self-consistent with each other: they come from different compilations, and the nucleus drawn here is the one the nuclear-volume source implies, not one derived from the cell. budget.mjs flags this rather than reconciling it.

rise_per_bp_nm.source: computed here from PDB 1BNA coordinates; see MACHINES.b_dna.rise_per_bp_nm
rise_per_bp_nm.citation: Drew, H.R., Wing, R.M., Takano, T., Broka, C., Tanaka, S., Itakura, K. & Dickerson, R.E. (1981) Structure of a B-DNA dodecamer: conformation and dynamics. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 78:2179-2183. doi:10.1073/pnas.78.4.2179 (PMID 6941276). PDB 1BNA, 1.9 A. Reports a 19 degree bend in the helix axis over the 11 base-pair steps, and a mean 36.9 degrees of rotation per step (9.8 bp/turn) in the centre of the molecule where the perturbation is least.

genome_bp.source: GRCh38.p14, assembly accession GCF_000001405.40, Homo sapiens. NCBI Datasets dataset_report: total_sequence_length 3,099,441,038 bp; total_ungapped_length 2,948,318,359 bp; 24 chromosomes; GC 41%.

nuclear_diameter_um.source: derived in CELL.nuclear_diameter from the 1,000 um^3 nuclear volume
nuclear_diameter_um.citation: Deviri, D. & Safran, S.A. (2022) Balance of osmotic pressures determines the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic volume ratio of the cell. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 119:e2118301119. doi:10.1073/pnas.2118301119 (PMID 35580183, PMC9173802). Uses a human nuclear volume of ~1,000 um^3 and computes the corresponding spherical radius of 6.2 um; attributes the volume to Guo et al. 2017.

duplex_diameter_nm.note: Low end is the conventional 2.0 nm, which this file does not claim as a retrieved value; high end is the atom-centre span measured from 1BNA. Carried as a bracket for exactly that reason.

compaction_factor.what_it_means: The length of double helix that has to be folded into one nuclear diameter. It is a ratio of a length to a length, not a packing density, and it says nothing about how the folding is done.

dna_volume_in_the_nucleus.the_point: Under one per cent. The compaction problem is a problem about LENGTH and topology, not about volume. There is no volume crisis in the nucleus, and a depiction that fills the nucleus solid with visible DNA is wrong by two orders of magnitude.

nucleosome_spacing_in_the_nucleus.the_point: Nucleosomes sit roughly three of their own diameters apart on average. So the nucleus is neither solid chromatin nor empty between the fibres: the ~20 nm gaps are filled by linker DNA, linker histone and nucleoplasmic protein, none of which this file has a measured concentration for.
nucleosome_spacing_in_the_nucleus.caveat: The 11 nm figure is the conventional disc diameter of a nucleosome core particle, which was NOT retrieved this session; the measured bounding box of 1KX5 is 12.2 x 15.5 x 7.2 nm including the extended histone tails. It is used only as a scale for the comparison.

what_was_not_computed.units: chromatin volume fraction in the nucleus
what_was_not_computed.null_reason: Chromatin is not naked DNA. Its volume includes histones, linker histone, every chromatin-associated protein and the hydration shell, and no measured nucleoplasmic macromolecule concentration was retrieved this session.
what_was_not_computed.what_would_resolve_it: A cryo-electron-tomography or quantitative-phase measurement of macromolecular mass density inside the nucleus of a named mammalian cell type, in g/mL.

what_this_rules_out.depiction: A sparse cytoplasm: machines drawn as separate objects with clear fluid visible between them.
what_this_rules_out.forbidden_by: CROWDING.microbe (0.3-0.4 g/mL of total macromolecules, measured) and CROWDING.mammalian (0.2 g/mL of protein alone, compiled), converted by SPECIFIC_VOLUME.
what_this_rules_out.why_it_bites: A mid-sized globular protein is 4-6 nm across and its nearest neighbour's centre is about 8.7 nm away. The average gap is roughly one protein diameter. There is no scale at which clear fluid is the right thing to draw between macromolecules.
what_this_rules_out.what_the_viewer_must_do_instead: Fill the volume to the stated fraction with unlabelled background macromolecules, and label that background as generated rather than placed - it is the honest way to be wrong.

what_this_rules_out.depiction: A nucleus with free space around the chromosomes - chromatin as discrete objects in clear nucleoplasm.
what_this_rules_out.forbidden_by: DNA_IN_THE_NUCLEUS.nucleosome_spacing_in_the_nucleus, together with the absence of any void in CROWDING.
what_this_rules_out.why_it_bites: Three diameters of mean separation is not free space, it is a crowded gel. And nothing in the nucleus is less crowded than the cytoplasm by any measurement retrieved here.
what_this_rules_out.what_the_viewer_must_do_instead: Draw chromatin at the measured spacing and fill the remainder with background macromolecules, saying that the non-DNA nuclear content has no retrieved concentration behind it.

what_this_rules_out.depiction: A ribosome drawn at whatever size makes it visible.
what_this_rules_out.forbidden_by: MACHINES.ribosome (measured bounding box and occupied volume) against MACHINES.ribosome.counts.human_cell_line and CELL.volume.
what_this_rules_out.why_it_bites: The headroom is under a factor of two in diameter, and it is only that large because the calculation generously gives ribosomes the entire protein volume budget. Enlarge a ribosome to make it legible and you have drawn a cell that is full of ribosomes and nothing else.
what_this_rules_out.what_the_viewer_must_do_instead: Keep the ribosome at its measured size and solve legibility with camera, colour and labelling, not with scale. If any object is drawn out of scale, say which and by how much.

what_this_rules_out.depiction: One nucleosome spacing drawn everywhere, and one rise per base pair.
what_this_rules_out.forbidden_by: MACHINES.nucleosome.spacing (193 bp in one primary cell type, 203 bp in another, 178-206 bp across chromatin states within one genome) and MACHINES.b_dna.rise_per_bp_nm.per_step_range_nm (2.817-4.017 A across eleven steps of one crystal structure).
what_this_rules_out.why_it_bites: These are not measurement error, they are biology. A single regular helix with evenly spaced beads depicts an average that no stretch of real chromatin equals.
what_this_rules_out.what_the_viewer_must_do_instead: Either vary the spacing within the measured range and say the variation is generated, or draw the average and label it as the average.

what_this_rules_out.depiction: A labelled "RNA polymerase" copied from the structure cited here.
what_this_rules_out.forbidden_by: MACHINES.rna_polymerase: PDB 5IYA is a 23-entity pre-initiation COMPLEX at 5.4 A, not a polymerase.
what_this_rules_out.why_it_bites: The viewer's whole claim is that its numbers are traceable. A mislabelled object breaks that claim more cheaply than a wrong number does, because nobody will check it.
what_this_rules_out.what_the_viewer_must_do_instead: Label it as the pre-initiation complex, or fetch a structure of the polymerase alone and run the same volume computation on it.

MEASURED.label: Measured
MEASURED.definition: A measurement reported in a cited publication or a public dataset, in a named organism and cell type.

DATABASE_RECORD.label: Database record
DATABASE_RECORD.definition: A specific record in a named public service, identified by accession and by the date it was retrieved.

TOOL_OUTPUT.label: Tool output
TOOL_OUTPUT.definition: Produced by a named piece of software at a named version. The tool, not the world, is the source.

DERIVED.label: Derived here
DERIVED.definition: Computed in this repo from other sourced claims, carrying the formula and the ids of its inputs.

DEPICTED.label: Depicted
DEPICTED.definition: Invented for the drawing - a position, an orientation, a colour, a count chosen to fit the frame. Carries no evidential weight and must say what it stands in for.

NOT_ESTABLISHED.label: Not established
NOT_ESTABLISHED.definition: We looked and could not source it. A labelled hole, with where we looked and what would fill it.

provenance_rule.one_line: DEPICTED is a kind of provenance, not a confession.
provenance_rule.why_it_is_first_class: A drawing of a ribosome inside a cell has to put the ribosome SOMEWHERE. There is no measurement of where that particular ribosome was at that particular instant, and no physics in this repo computes one, so the position comes out of a layout function. That is true of every molecular illustration ever published, including the ones on the covers of the textbooks. The choice available is not between invented positions and measured ones; it is between invented positions that are labelled and invented positions that are not.
provenance_rule.what_goes_wrong_without_it: Without a DEPICTED kind there are two bad outcomes and no good one. Either the position is given a fake source - the paper that measured the ribosome DIAMETER gets cited for the ribosome POSITION, because it was the nearest citation to hand - or the position carries no provenance at all, which in a view where everything else carries provenance reads as an oversight rather than as a claim about invention. Both make the view less honest than simply saying: we put it there.
provenance_rule.what_it_buys: Separability. A reader can ask of any element on screen: is this a thing someone measured, or a thing we drew? share() answers that for a whole view in one number with a named numerator, so a view that is nine-tenths invention says so above the fold instead of in a footnote. And a designer using this viewer to build an organism can see exactly which of the things they are reasoning about are load-bearing and which are scenery.
provenance_rule.the_hard_part: A DEPICTED claim must say WHAT IT IS STANDING IN FOR, and that is the field people want to leave blank. "Position of a ribosome" is not an answer; "the position of one of the roughly 6500 ribosomes this cell is modelled as having, chosen so that the local density matches the count and the volume" is. cite() throws without it, because a depiction that cannot say what it depicts is not a depiction, it is decoration.
provenance_rule.and_the_counts: The same applies to counts chosen to fit a frame. If the view draws forty ribosomes because forty is what renders at 60 fps, that forty is DEPICTED and the real count is a separate MEASURED or NOT_ESTABLISHED claim that the depiction cites. cite() refuses a DEPICTED claim carrying a number for exactly this reason: a number on screen gets quoted, and the label travels with the position.
